title: Renewal runway & usage heatmap worksheet
body:
Purpose: a lightweight working worksheet to use in QBRs that summarizes token velocity, short-term runway, rate-limit incidents, and suggested immediate mitigations. This is meant to be editable during preparation calls and to feed one-slide QBR summaries.

Sheet layout (columns) — when converting to a spreadsheet tab:
- Customer
- Plan (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)
- Month (YYYY-MM)
- Total tokens consumed (numeric)
- Avg tokens per request (numeric)
- Requests (count)
- Peak RPS (requests/sec)
- Rate-limit events (count)
- Percent requests throttled (formula: Rate-limit events / Requests)
- Token burn rate (tokens/day formula: Total tokens / days_in_month)
- 30-day runway (days) — formula: If monthly budget_tokens > 0 then (budget_tokens - month_to_date_tokens) / (token_burn_rate) else blank
- Budget_tokens (customer-configured monthly token allowance)
- Estimated overage $ (approx) — formula: max(0, (month_to_date_tokens - budget_tokens) * unit_price_per_token)
- Renewal risk score (0-100) — see scoring rules below
- Suggested mitigation (short text)
- Next action owner
- Notes / evidence links

Sample rows (example data to copy into your QBR prep):
- Acme Inc., Hosted, 2026-01, 18,540,000, 1,200, 15,000, 120, 0.008, 598, 50,000, 6,480.00, 72, "apply burst policy + token-trim prompts", Marcus Nguyen, "Spike tied to marketing campaign; see ticket JIRA-CS-710"
- BrightStore, Dedicated, 2026-01, 3,200,000, 650, 4,900, 9, 0.0018, 103, 30,000, 0.00, 18, "increase rate-limit cap for dedicated pool; schedule canary", Priya Shah, "pending capacity change request"
- EmberApps, Private, 2026-01, 62,000,000, 2,400, 25,800, 980, 0.038, 2,000, 150,000, 12400.00, 85, "discounted overage + dedicated burst window", Diego Ramirez, "ongoing exploratory cache rollout"

Alerting & threshold guidance (QBR-ready):
- Green: 30-day runway > 21 days AND percent requests throttled < 0.5% AND estimated overage <$500.
- Yellow: runway 7–21 days OR percent throttled between 0.5%–2% OR estimated overage $500–$5k.
- Red: runway < 7 days OR percent throttled > 2% OR estimated overage >$5k.
- Escalation path: yellow -> CS lead + Solutions Eng (SWE) review within 3 business days; red -> immediate capacity/discount pause conversation + finance engaged.

Renewal risk scoring (suggested heuristic, tunable):
- Base score 50. Add/subtract based on:
  - Runway: if <7d add 20; 7–21d add 10; >21d subtract 5.
  - Throttling: if >2% add 20; 0.5–2% add 10.
  - Overage: if >$5k add 15; $500–$5k add 5.
  - Support volume: if >5 priority incidents in last 90d add 10.
  - Contract value: top-tier customers subtract 10.
- Cap score to 0–100. Map to simple labels for slides: 0–30 Low, 31–60 Medium, 61–100 High.

Suggested mitigations (quick snippets you can paste into a QBR action tracker):
- Token trimming + prompt engineering: supply 1–2 example prompt edits that cut token count by ~30% (attach prompt diff).
- Burst window: enable temporary burst capacity for 72 hours while customer adjusts client-side throttles.
- Rate-limit policy change: increase per-route limits on Dedicated pools (requires infra approval).
- Caching: enable per-prefix KV cache for repeated prompts (estimate: if cache-hit >30% expect 25–45% token reduction).
- Billing adjustment: offer one-time credit for campaign-driven spikes and present a revised renewal commit to smooth long-term churn risk.

QBR slide talking points (1-line bullets):
- 1) Past period highlight: total tokens vs committed allowance (call out % over/under).
- 2) Incident summary: # rate limit events, root cause & fix status.
- 3) Runway & risk: 30-day runway and renewal risk score + recommended mitigation.
- 4) Ask: short-term capacity change (yes/no), ask for commit change, or engineering action items.

Quick formulas and snippets for sheet implementers:
- Percent throttled: =if(B2>0, H2 / F2, 0)  -- where H = rate-limit events, F = requests.
- Token burn (per day): =D2 / DAYS(EOMONTH(C2,0) - C2 + 1)  -- D=total tokens, C=month date.
- 30-day runway: =if(L2>0, (L2 - G2) / I2, "n/a") -- L=budget_tokens, G=month_to_date_tokens, I=token_burn_rate.
- Estimated overage $: =max(0, (G2 - L2) * unit_price)  -- unit_price held in a named cell.

Operational notes for CS leads preparing the sheet:
- Pull tokens and request counts from billing export + usage API; cross-check top N routes for high token density.
- Reconcile with support logs for rate-limit events (use trace_id to link incidents).
- If a spike maps to a marketing event, tag it as "campaign" and recommend one-time credit in QBR.
- Keep one column with a timestamped link to related PRs/infra tickets.

Meeting choreography (how to use in a QBR):
- 5 min: one-slide summary from this sheet (green/yellow/red).
- 10–15 min: if yellow/red, dive into top 3 drivers (routes, dates, campaigns).
- 5 min: agree next steps + owner + ETA.

Additional sections to add when turning into a multi-tab workbook:
- Tab A: raw usage export (daily granularity)
- Tab B: high-token routes (top 20 by tokens)
- Tab C: incident timeline (rate-limit events mapped to support tickets)
- Tab D: pricing & commit mapping (unit price, committed tokens, effective rates)
- Tab E: recommendations log (action items, owners, status)

Notes (loose ends / TODOs):
- Add integration example for automated extraction from billing S3 export.
- Build a small script to generate the heatmap image for slide export (prefer PNG 1200x600).
- Validate the runway formula for customers who prepay tokens across quarters.

This is a working draft — use freely, add rows for each renewal cohort, and surface the single most urgent ask per customer on the front slide.
summary: Working worksheet to compute token runway, rate-limit exposure, simple renewal risk score, and recommended short-term mitigations for QBRs. Designed for Customer Success teams to prepare a one-slide summary and action tracker.
